title: Winter Games
build: Epyx original, PAL, two disk sides (C64 Preservation Project, verified dump)

records.c: Sprite shapes $90-$96 (the video chip's bank 1, $4000-$7FFF, shape n at $4000 + 64n): the flame catching in the cauldron, left halves $90-$93 and right halves $94-$96 (anim_flame_grow). Every shape from here to $7FFF is a multicolour sprite, 24 by 21, three bytes a row.
Shapes $97-$9F: the three big flags, three shapes each, flying on the poles at the top right (anim_flag_1 to anim_flag_3).

Shapes $A0-$A7, the torch bearer's first running frame, eight sprites: his head and body in $A0 and $A2 side by side, his legs in $A4 and $A6, and each one's hires outline in the shape after it ($A1, $A3, $A5, $A7), which prepare_bearer lays over the multicolour shape.
Shapes $A8-$AF, the second running frame, laid out like spr_bearer_run_0.
Shapes $B0-$B7, the third running frame.
Shapes $B8-$BF, the fourth running frame.
Shapes $C0-$C7, the fifth running frame.
Shapes $C8-$CF, the sixth running frame.
Shapes $D0-$D7, the seventh running frame.
Shapes $D8-$DF, the eighth running frame.
Shapes $E0-$E7, the ninth running frame.
Shapes $E8-$EF, the tenth and last running frame.
Shapes $F0-$F7: the torch bearer standing at the top of the steps, laid out like a running frame (anim_bearer_pose_top, anim_bearer_stand_top).

Shapes $F8-$FF: the torch bearer raising the torch, shown for 48 steps of anim_bearer_pose_top. Once he is standing again, bearer_run copies the big flame and the doves over $7E40-$8006, so only $F8 keeps this pose; $F9-$FF become spr_big_flame and spr_doves.
Shapes $F9-$FB as they load, part of the raised torch (spr_bearer_raise): bearer_run's copy from spr_big_flame starts here, 256 bytes in its first loop.
Shapes $FD-$FF as they load, the raised torch's legs: bearer_run's second copy loop, 199 bytes from $A811, starts here and runs on to $8006.

512 bytes nothing reads, shaped like eight sprites (three bytes a row), past the end of the video chip's bank, where it cannot show them. bearer_run's copy runs seven bytes past the doves and writes $8000-$8006.

File O's entry, where the loader's JMP at $0B07 lands: interrupts off, the processor port's direction register to $2F and the port to $05 (BASIC and the KERNAL banked out, the I/O chips in), then on to opening_start.
Two zero bytes. eng_ptr_a and eng_ptr_b both hold this address.
The address $820C, which opening_start copies to $04-$05. Nothing in this part reads $04-$05 or this word again.
The high byte of eng_ptr_a.
The address $820C again; nothing in this part reads it.

The inner loop of fill_bytes: stores A at the address in its own operand (fill_ptr), moves the operand on, and counts $56 (low) and $57 (high) down; it stops when $57 goes below zero, so it stores $57 * 256 + $56 bytes.
The operand of fill_store's STA, the next address to fill, set by fill_bytes and moved on by fill_store itself.
The high byte of fill_store's operand, moved on every 256 bytes.
Fills memory with one value: from $58-$59, value in $5A, count in $56-$57 (fill_store). clear_actors uses it to clear the actor records.
Makes the 16-bit number in $63-$64 positive, negating it when its high byte is negative.
Multiplies $B1 by $B0 into $63-$64, shift and add, eight rounds. Nothing in this part calls it: the engine is shared with the events, and this is one of its routines the opening has no use for.

How many steps the current actor (record at $5E) is owed: the frames since its last step, $4D minus offset 6, divided by offset 8 (frames per step) and capped at offset 9, into $6B. With its timer on (bit 7 of offset $0C) it takes the steps off the 16-bit timer at offsets $0A-$0B; when that runs out it sets bit 3 of offset $2E, the event that wakes the actor, and owes no steps.

One step of the current actor: anim_advance, then the motion. Velocity takes on acceleration (offsets $19-$1A plus $1D-$1E across, $1B-$1C plus $23-$24 down), and the position takes on velocity: across as fraction, low byte and a ninth bit ($39, $3A, $3B, for the sprite's X register and its high bit), down as fraction and line ($3C, $3D). With offset $52 set, the actor moves only on the step its animation frame's countdown (offset $3E) is 0, so a walking figure steps with its frames instead of sliding.
Runs act_step as many times as act_due_steps found ($6B), then stamps the actor with the frame clock $4D at offset 6.
Puts $63-$64 into the current actor's timer, offsets $0A-$0B.

Sets the current actor's timer to $63-$64 steps and turns it on (bit 7 of offset $0C); act_due_steps counts it down and wakes the actor when it runs out. Every actor script here sets one and then waits with act_wait.
Turns the current actor's timer off (clears bit 7 of offset $0C).
Returns bit 3 of offset $2E, set when the actor's timer ran out. Unused here, like the next three: a second timer the engine keeps for the events.
Puts $63-$64 at offsets $0E-$0F, a second timer. Unused here.
act_timer2_value and bit 4 of offset $0C. Unused here.
Returns bit 4 of offset $2E. Unused here.
Puts the current actor at column $63-$64 (sprite X coordinates, offset $3A and its ninth bit at $3B), with the fraction at $39 cleared.
Puts the current actor on line $63 (offset $3D, sprite Y coordinates), with the fraction at $3C cleared.
Sets the current actor's speed across to $63-$64 (offsets $19-$1A), in 256ths of a pixel per step.
Sets the current actor's speed down to $63-$64 (offsets $1B-$1C), in 256ths of a line per step.
Sets the acceleration across, offsets $1D-$1E. Unused here.
Sets the acceleration down, offsets $23-$24. Unused here.
Stops the current actor: both speeds to 0.
Both accelerations and both speeds to 0. Unused here.
Puts the current actor at column 0, line 0. Unused here.

Keeps the current actor inside its box, for the actors that turn it on (bit 0 of offset $0C; none does in this part). Across (bit 1 of offset $0D) against $1F-$20 and $21-$22, down (bit 2) against $25 and $27: an actor past an edge is put one pixel inside it, and the edge it hit is noted in offset $2F (1 bottom, 2 top, 4 right, 8 left) with bit 0 of $2E, which wakes it.
Sets bit 0 of offset $2E, the "hit an edge" event.
Past the right edge: event, bit 2 of offset $2F, and back to one pixel left of it.
Past the left edge: event, bit 3 of offset $2F, and back to one pixel right of it.
Past the bottom edge: event, bit 0 of offset $2F, and back to one line above it.
Past the top edge: event, bit 1 of offset $2F, and back to one line below it.
The box's left edge, offsets $1F-$20, from $63-$64. Unused here, with the rest of the box routines to act_bumped.
The box's right edge, offsets $21-$22.
The box's top line, offset $25.
The box's bottom line, offset $27.
Turns on the box across (bit 0 of offset $0C, bit 1 of $0D).
Turns on the box down (bit 0 of offset $0C, bit 2 of $0D).
Turns the box and the timer off (bit 7 of offset $0C, bits 1 and 2 of $0D).
Returns the top and bottom edges hit, bits 0-1 of offset $2F.
Returns the left and right edges hit, bits 2-3 of offset $2F.
Returns bit 0 of offset $2E, any edge hit.
Reverses the current actor's speed across (offsets $19-$1A); the speeds in the tables are given positive and turned round here.
Reverses the current actor's speed down (offsets $1B-$1C).
Bounces off the edges hit: reverses the speed across after a left or right edge, the speed down after a top or bottom one. Unused here.
A flag, 0 here: sched_next returns from sched_run when it, or $A8, is not 0. Nothing in this part sets either.

Starts an actor: called from the start of an actor's script, it takes its own return address off the stack and stores it in the record at $60 (offsets $36-$37) as the place to resume, marks the record active and due to resume (offset 0 = 6), and returns to whoever called the script. The rest of the script then runs as the actor, from sched_run.
act_due_steps, then act_take_steps when steps are owed.

The actors' scheduler, which never returns in this part: one pass over every actor record from number $65 (11) down to 0 through the address table at $33 (act_list), again and again. An actor flagged inactive (bit 1 of offset 0 clear) is passed over; one due to resume (bit 2) is entered at the address its script saved; any other is moved (act_move, or only its clock with bit 5), kept in its box, and marked due to resume when any event bit of offset $2E is set. Between actors it looks at both joysticks and the keyboard, and anything pressed leaves for the loader's $0900, which loads the menu.
The scheduler's loop for one actor: the check of sched_halt and $A8, the joysticks and the keyboard, then the record's own turn.
Any key or joystick during the ceremony: on to the loader's restart, $0900, which loads the menu.
Where every routine that ends an actor's turn comes back: the next record down, or a new pass from $65.
A JMP to sched_next that nothing reaches.
Ends the current actor's turn and puts it to sleep (bit 1 of offset 0 cleared, bit 0 set) until act_wake; the return address is kept as where it resumes. Unused here.
Wakes the actor whose record is at $60: active and due to resume. Unused here.
Ends the current actor for good (offset 0 = 0) and goes on with the scheduler. Unused here.
Four actor records in two pairs, $1564 and $15B8, then $1660 and $16B4, for act_find_free. Nothing in this part reads them.
act_pairs: the high byte of the first record of the first pair.
act_pairs: the second record of the first pair, low byte.
act_pairs: the high byte of the first pair's second record.
act_pairs: the first record of the second pair, low byte.
act_pairs: the high byte of the second pair's first record.
act_pairs: the second record of the second pair, low byte.
act_pairs: the high byte of the second pair's second record.
Which pair act_find_free looks in (0 the first).
Points $60-$61 at the first record of the chosen pair whose offset 0 is 0, a free actor, or sets $61 to 0 when both are busy. Unused here.
Ends the current actor's turn to wait for an event without moving or animating (bit 5): its timer still counts. Like act_wait otherwise. Unused here.

Ends the current actor's turn until an event: shown (bit 7 of offset 0), not due to resume, with its return address kept at $36-$37 as where to resume. Its events are cleared, it is stamped with the frame clock, and a speed divider or step limit of 0 becomes 1. The scheduler moves and animates it meanwhile; a timer running out (act_timer_start) or an edge (act_bounds) wakes it.
Hides the current actor (clears bit 7 of offset 0). Unused here.
Shows the current actor (sets bit 7 of offset 0). Unused here.
The same as act_hide. Unused here.

The colour of each sprite shape, from shape $90 on ($6400), which anim_show gives a frame's sprites: 0 (black) for $94 and $97-$9C, 6 (blue) for $9D-$9F, 7 (yellow) for the rest. 136 bytes, more than this part's 112 shapes.
The address of spr_colours, which opening_start puts in $FB-$FC for anim_show.
The high byte of spr_colours_ptr.
Sets the current actor's two sprite colours from spr_colours by the shapes at offsets $11 and $12, without anim_show's subtraction of $90. Unused here.

Gives the current actor the animation at $80-$81 and shows its first frame. The animation's first byte holds the flags: bit 7 for a list of animations to choose from (anim_choose), bit 4 for frames that last a set number of steps, and the low bits for the second sprite (offset $32): 0 none, 1 below the first, 2 to its right, 3 over it.
Sets offset $15, the value anim_choose chooses by. Unused here.
For a list of animations: picks the entry whose range holds offset $15 and makes it the actor's animation. Unused here.
Back to frame 0 (offset $2A).

Shows the current frame: the frame's record, five bytes from offset 2 of the animation, gives the first sprite's shape (offset $11) and, when not 0, the second's (offset $12), with each one's colour from spr_colours; then how long the frame lasts, as steps for a timed animation (offsets $3E-$3F) or as distance for the others (offsets $16-$17).
Reads the frame record's fifth byte and returns whatever it holds: the byte is 0 in every animation here, and nothing uses it.

Moves the current actor's animation on by one step, when it has one: a timed frame counts its steps down (offsets $3E-$3F); the others count down the distance moved (offsets $16-$17), taking off one of the two speeds made positive (abs_arg). The choice of speed is meant to be the larger, but the comparison reads offset $1B, the low byte of the speed down, where its high byte at $1C belongs; every animation in this part is timed, so the slip never shows here. When the count runs out the next frame is shown, and after the last (the animation's second byte) the first again.

Reads offsets $48-$49 into $80-$81, a screen address. This routine and the five after it save, draw and restore a block of three by three characters on a text screen at $4800 for an actor: none runs in this part, which shows a bitmap.
Points $84-$85 at offset $4A of the current actor's record, nine bytes kept there.
Writes $80-$81 to offsets $48-$49.

Draws nine characters from ($84) on the screen at ($80), three rows of three, with each one's colour from a zero-page table at $A2, indexed by the character, plus 8 (multicolour), written to colour RAM at the screen address plus $9000, which is $D800 for a screen at $4800.
Moves cells_draw and cells_save one character on, and to the next row (40 on) after three; after the ninth it leaves its caller's loop by dropping a return address.
Saves the nine characters at ($80) in the actor's record (act_cells_buffer).

The flag on the third pole: shapes $97, $98, $99, $98, each lasting 14, 11, 10 and 12 steps (flag $10, timed; one sprite). Every animation is laid out alike: flags, last frame, then five bytes a frame (shape, second shape or 0, two bytes of length, a byte nothing reads).
The flag on the first pole: shapes $9A, $9B, $9C, $9B, lasting 9, 15, 12 and 14 steps.
The flag on the second pole: shapes $9D, $9E, $9F, $9E, lasting 14, 11, 15 and 12 steps.
The addresses of the three flag animations, which start_actors gives the three flag actors.
The high byte of anim_flag_1's address.
The address of anim_flag_2, for the first flag actor; low byte.
The high byte of anim_flag_2's address.
The address of anim_flag_3, for the second flag actor; low byte.
The high byte of anim_flag_3's address.
The flame catching in the cauldron: two sprites side by side (flags $12), shapes $90 and $94, $91 and $94, $92 and $95, $93 and $96, for 20, 22, 24 and 25 steps.

The flame burning, eight frames that loop: $92 and $95, $93 and $96, $F9 and $FA (the big flame copied in by bearer_run), $93 and $95, $92 and $96, $F9 and $FA, $92 and $95, $93 and $96, 13 to 15 steps each.
The addresses of the two flame animations, for flame_start.
The high byte of anim_flame_grow's address.
The address of anim_flame_flicker, low byte.
The high byte of anim_flame_flicker's address.

The torch bearer's head and body running, ten frames of three steps: shapes $A0 and $A2, $A8 and $AA, and so on 8 apart to $E8 and $EA. Each shape has a hires outline in the next shape up, which prepare_bearer lays over it.
The torch bearer's legs running, the same ten frames: $A4 and $A6 to $EC and $EE.
The addresses of the two running animations, for bearer_top_start and bearer_legs_start.
The high byte of anim_bearer_run_top's address.
The address of anim_bearer_run_legs, low byte.
The high byte of anim_bearer_run_legs' address.
The torch bearer at the top of the steps: standing ($F0 and $F2) for 96 steps, the torch raised ($F8 and $FA) for 48, then standing again in nine frames of 240.
The address of anim_bearer_pose_top, read by bearer_run.
The high byte of anim_bearer_pose_top_ptr.
The legs under anim_bearer_pose_top: $F4 and $F6, $FC and $FE, then $F4 and $F6, with the same lengths.
The address of anim_bearer_pose_legs.
The high byte of anim_bearer_pose_legs_ptr.
A dove flapping: shapes $FB, $FC, $FD, $FE, $FF, $FD, a step each (one sprite, timed). The shapes are in place once bearer_run has copied them in.
The address of anim_dove, read by dove_start.
The high byte of anim_dove_ptr.
The torch bearer standing for good, $F0 and $F2, three frames of 240 steps.
The address of anim_bearer_stand_top.
The high byte of anim_bearer_stand_top_ptr.
The legs standing for good, $F4 and $F6.
The address of anim_bearer_stand_legs.
The high byte of anim_bearer_stand_legs_ptr.
The twelve actor records' addresses, $1510 to $1900, $54 bytes apart with $160C left out, which eng_init copies to $13-$2A for the interrupts' sprite drawing.
The same twelve addresses, which eng_init copies to $33-$4A for the scheduler.
Sets $0A-$0C to $65, $FA and $DD (the raster lines of the first interrupts; $0C is not read here) and copies the two tables of actor addresses to zero page.

The ceremony's picture, its bitmap packed for unpack_stream: 5,090 bytes that unpack to the 8,000 at $4000-$5F3F, over the title picture. The first two bytes are the destination. From here, bitmap rows 0-4: the sky and the snowy mountains.
The packed bitmap continued, from row 4: the mountains and the ten small flags on their poles behind the stands.
The packed bitmap continued, from row 7: the crowd in the stands.
The packed bitmap continued, from row 10: the stands' front, the track and the cauldron.
The packed bitmap continued, from row 14: the cauldron's stand and the steps.
The packed bitmap continued, from row 21 to its end at $A05A: the foot of the steps and the snow.
The packed bitmap continued, across $A000, where the BASIC ROM sits when it is banked in; it is banked out while the ceremony runs.
The picture's screen memory packed: 541 bytes that unpack to the 1,000 at $6000-$63E7, two colours for each character cell.
The picture's colour RAM packed: 361 bytes that unpack to the 1,000 at $D800-$DBE7, each cell's third colour.
The addresses of the three packed streams, which unpack_picture reads in turn.
The high byte of the bitmap stream's address.
The screen stream's address, low byte.
The high byte of the screen stream's address.
The colour stream's address, low byte.
The high byte of the colour stream's address.
Unpacks the ceremony's picture: bitmap, screen and colours, from the three streams in pic_streams.
Unpacks the stream whose address is at $B4 + X in zero page. Unused here.
Unpacks each stream named in a list at ($AB), two bytes an address, until an address of 0. Unused here.

Unpacks the stream at ($A9): two bytes of destination (into $B2-$B3), then commands, each a byte whose top two bits say what to do with the count in its low six. 0: the next byte, count times (a count of 0 ends the stream); 1: the next count bytes as they are; 2: leave count bytes as they were; 3: count bytes, each followed by two zeros. This part's streams use only 0 and 1.
Moves the destination pointer $B2-$B3 on by one.
Moves the stream pointer $A9-$AA on by one.
Starts a flag: animation $80-$81, column $84-$85, line $82, then act_start; as an actor it waits on act_wait with no timer, so it never wakes and flies its flag for good.
An act_sleep after the flag's act_wait, which no event ever wakes it to reach.

Starts the flame in the cauldron, actor 8. As an actor it waits 712 steps, shows anim_flame_grow at column 62, line 125 for 93 steps, then anim_flame_flicker for good. A step is a frame here: the clock at $4D goes up once a frame in irq_bottom, and every actor's divider and step limit are 1.
Another act_sleep that act_wait never returns to.

Starts dove number offset $50 (0-4), actors 3-7. Each waits its turn (dove_delay, 778 to 926 steps), then flies anim_dove from column 5, line 89, up and to the right at its own speeds, checking every second step whether it has gone off the top (its line wrapped round to 200 or more); then it starts again from the left.
The five doves' first waits, low bytes: 778, 820, 844, 879 and 926 steps with dove_delay_hi.
The first waits' high bytes, all 3.
The doves' starting line, 89 for each.
Five zeros, read with dove_y into $64, which act_set_y does not use.
The doves' starting column, 5 for each, low bytes.
The starting columns' high bytes, 0.
The doves' climbing speeds in 256ths of a line a step, low bytes: 100, 80, 65, 120, 140; dove_start turns them upward.
The climbing speeds' high bytes, 0.
The doves' speeds across, low bytes: with dove_vx_hi 436, 506, 476, 572 and 602 256ths of a pixel a step.
The speeds' high bytes, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2.
Starts the torch bearer's upper half, actor 9: anim_bearer_run_top at line 185, stopping its climb above line 150.
Starts the torch bearer's legs, actor 10: anim_bearer_run_legs at line 206, stopping above line 171, 21 lines under the upper half.

The torch bearer's script, for both halves: off the right edge (column 344) it waits 250 steps, runs in to the left at 7 pixels a move until it is left of column 256, then climbs the steps up and to the left at 356 256ths of a line a move until its line is above offset $51, and stops. With offset $52 set it moves only once a frame of its animation, every fourth step. Then it stands, raises the torch, waits 192 steps and copies the big flame and the doves from $A711-$A8D7 over shapes $F9-$FF; then it stands for good. Each half makes the copy, the second over the first.
The act_sleep after the torch bearer's last act_wait, never reached.
Two shapes that bearer_run copies to $7E40 to become shapes $F9 and $FA: the big flame, left and right, two frames of anim_flame_flicker.
Five shapes that become $FB-$FF: a dove with its wings at five places in a beat (anim_dove).
The third to fifth dove shapes, $FD-$FF once copied, and the start of bearer_run's second copy loop, which takes 199 bytes from here, seven past the last dove.
1 while irq_flame draws its one actor, so that draw_actors stops after it; 0 otherwise. Also the first of the seven bytes bearer_run's copy takes past the doves.
A JMP to opening_start that nothing reaches.
Sets the background black and fills 1,001 bytes from $4000 with 0 (fill_bytes). Unused here.
irq_bottom's loop counter over the ten small flags.
Each small flag's countdown to its next frame, in frames.
Each small flag's frame, as an offset into its 24 bytes; it steps 8, 16, 8, 0 and round again.
Each small flag's frames between pictures, 8 to 26, all different so that they do not flap together.
The bitmap cells the small flags are drawn in, low bytes: every fourth cell of row 5, columns 3 to 39.
The cells' high bytes, $46 and $47.

The raster interrupt at line 240 (250 the first time), the first of three a frame. It counts the frame on the clock at $4D, sets the next interrupt for line 101 (irq_flame), and flaps the ten small flags behind the stands: each flag whose countdown runs out has the next of its three pictures copied into its bitmap cell. Then a step of the tune (music_step), the torch bearer's sprites worked out for later (prepare_bearer), and the sprites for the top of the screen: the three big flags and the five doves, one sprite each (draw_actors).

Puts actors into sprites, from the actor at ($4F), number $69/2 in the list at $13: A is the multicolour mask for $D01C. Each shown actor (bit 7 of its offset 0) gets its column, line and shape from offsets $3A-$3B, $3D and $11, and its colour from $30; its second sprite (offsets $12 and $31) goes beside, below or over the first by offset $32 when the interrupt draws one actor or prepares the torch bearer, and is left out at the top of the screen. A hidden actor leaves two sprites unused. It stops after one actor (irq_one_actor), after eight actors at the top of the screen (eight_sprites, which then sets fixed colours: black, white, orange and five white), or after four actors when preparing the torch bearer.
The fixed colours for the top of the screen, which replace the actors' own: sprite 0 black, 1 white, 2 orange, 3-7 white.

The end of draw_actors. When preparing the torch bearer it copies his four sprites to sprites 4-7 as well, sets sprites 0-3 to the next shape up (the hires outlines), keeps the positions, the ninth bits and the shapes in bearer_regs, bearer_msb and bearer_ptrs, and returns to irq_bottom; otherwise it leaves the interrupt.
Restores Y, X and A and returns from the interrupt.

The raster interrupt at line 101: sets the next for line 141 (irq_bearer), takes a step of the tune, and puts the flame (actor 8, two sprites side by side) into sprites 0 and 1, all multicolour, with red and orange as the shared colours.

The raster interrupt at line 141: sets the next for line 240 (irq_bottom) and shows the torch bearer worked out by prepare_bearer, eight sprites: multicolour sprites 4-7 in yellow with light blue and orange, under hires outlines 0-3 in blue.
The torch bearer's eight sprite positions, X and Y for sprites 0-7, as prepare_bearer worked them out for irq_bearer.
The torch bearer's eight sprite shapes, for the pointers at $63F8-$63FF.
Four bytes after bearer_ptrs that nothing uses.
The torch bearer's ninth bits of X, for $D010.
Works out the torch bearer's sprites during irq_bottom: draw_actors from actor 9 with bearer_pending set, which keeps the result for irq_bearer instead of showing it.
1 while prepare_bearer runs draw_actors, which then keeps the sprites for irq_bearer and returns.
1 while irq_bottom draws the top of the screen, where draw_actors stops after eight sprites.
The addresses of irq_bottom and irq_flame, which opening_start copies to $0D-$0E and $0F-$10; irq_flame then sets $FFFE to irq_bearer, and irq_bearer to $0D-$0E.
The high byte of irq_bottom's address.
irq_flame's address, low byte.
The high byte of irq_flame's address.

The ceremony's start-up: marks the menu as overwritten for the loader ($083D = $FF, and $085F), the stack reset; engine and tune player set up (eng_init, music_init); then the KERNAL banked out, the timer interrupts off, the raster interrupt at line 250 to irq_bottom, the screen blanked, multicolour bitmap from video bank 1 (bitmap $4000, screen $6000), black border and background, twelve actors ($65 = 11), and the picture unpacked (unpack_picture). Then start_actors.
Clears the actor records, 1,092 bytes from $1510 (fill_bytes): thirteen places of $54 bytes, the twelve of act_list and the one at $160C that it leaves out.

Starts the ceremony's eleven actors: three flags (flag_start) at columns 246, 270 and 294, lines 74, 71 and 68; five doves; the flame; the torch bearer's two halves. Then the picture is shown ($D011 = $3B), the tune at offset 2 of tunes starts, and the scheduler runs.
A loop on itself after sched_run, which never returns in this part.
The low bytes of the small flags' pictures, one address for each of the ten (cell_frames).
The high bytes of the small flags' pictures.
The ten small flags' pictures, three for each: 24 bytes a flag, a bitmap cell of 8 bytes a picture.
22 bytes nothing reads, in the pattern of $3F, $C0 and $FF that fills the gaps of the title's file too.

Silences the SID and sets it up: every voice attack 2, decay 1, sustain 8, release 4, pulse width $400, volume 15; no tune playing ($FF in tune_now, the tune pointer $08-$09 at tune_none). Its last LDA #$FF is also the player's two variables: note_wait is its opcode and tune_now its operand, which works because music_init runs once, before music_step first writes $B030.
Calls of music_step left until the next note; the opcode of music_init's LDA #$FF until then.
The number of the tune playing (its offset in tunes), $FF for none; the operand of music_init's LDA #$FF.
Starts tune Y (an offset into tunes) unless the tune playing has a lower number: the tune pointer at $08-$09, and the first note at once.

The tune player, called twice a frame (irq_bottom and irq_flame). While a note lasts it counts note_wait down, and turns the gates off for its last four calls: voices 1 and 2 to pulse, voice 3 to sawtooth, the waveforms the other way round from the gates on, so each note's release sounds in another tone. Then the next record of four bytes: bit 7 of the first ends the tune; a first byte of 0 is a rest; otherwise three notes, one for each voice, from note_freq_lo and note_freq_hi (0 is silent), with voices 1 and 2 sawtooth and voice 3 pulse; the fourth byte picks the length from note_lengths.
The end of a tune: all three frequencies 0, tune_now $FF.
The tunes' addresses: offset 0, tune_other; offset 2, tune_ceremony.
The high bytes of the tunes' addresses, read with tunes by music_start.
The tune the ceremony plays from start_actors on, records of four bytes (three notes and a length) to the end mark at $B23B.
A second tune in the same form, to its end mark at $B394. Nothing in this part plays it.
An end mark on its own, where music_init points the player so that it plays nothing.

The SID frequencies of 48 notes, low bytes: 0 for silence, then C sharp 2 to B 5 a semitone apart. They are exact for an NTSC machine's clock (A 4 = 440 Hz at note 33); on a PAL machine, whose clock is 3.7 % slower, every note sounds about two-thirds of a semitone flat.
The frequencies' high bytes.
The note lengths, in calls of music_step (two a frame), by the tune's fourth byte: 192, 96, 144, 48, 72, 24, 36, 16, 80, 32, 12 and others.
